moses.title: Moses
moses.sub: From the Nile to Mount Nebo: signs, wonders and your notes
moses.how: This companion follows Moses from his birth in Egypt to his death on Mount Nebo. The ten plagues are numbered 1–10, and the other signs God did through Moses are lettered A–L, so you can see the whole pattern of God's power at a glance. Dates follow the early (traditional) dating of the Exodus, about 1446 BC; many scholars prefer a date in the 1200s BC. Each entry notes where the New Testament draws on the story.

phases.title: Born in Egypt
phases.intro: A new king who knew not Joseph made the Hebrews slaves and ordered their baby boys thrown into the Nile.

entries.title: Born under Pharaoh's decree
entries.text: Pharaoh ordered every Hebrew son cast into the river, but the midwives feared God, and a Levite mother hid her beautiful son for three months.

entries.title: Drawn out of the water
entries.text: Placed in an ark of bulrushes, he was found by Pharaoh's daughter, nursed by his own mother, and named Moses, for I drew him out of the water.

entries.title: He strikes an Egyptian and flees
entries.text: Seeing an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, Moses killed him. When it became known, he fled from Pharaoh to the land of Midian.

phases.title: Forty Years in Midian
phases.intro: Moses became a shepherd and family man in the wilderness, until God met him at the burning bush.

entries.title: Shepherd and son-in-law of Jethro
entries.text: Moses defended Jethro's daughters at a well, married Zipporah and kept his father-in-law's flocks. Meanwhile God heard Israel's groaning and remembered his covenant.

entries.title: The burning bush
entries.meta: Horeb, the mountain of God · Exodus 3:1–15
entries.text: A bush burned with fire and was not consumed. God called Moses by name, revealed himself as I AM THAT I AM, and sent him to bring Israel out of Egypt.

entries.title: The rod, the hand and the water
entries.text: God gave Moses signs to show the people: his rod became a serpent, his hand became leprous and was restored, and water would turn to blood. Aaron was appointed to speak for him.

phases.title: The Ten Plagues
phases.intro: Moses and Aaron told Pharaoh, Let my people go. Through ten plagues God executed judgment on the gods of Egypt (Exodus 12:12).

entries.title: Pharaoh refuses; bricks without straw
entries.text: Pharaoh answered, Who is Jehovah? and made the slaves' work harder. God renewed his promise: I will take you to me for a people.

entries.title: Aaron's rod swallows the magicians' rods
entries.text: Aaron's rod became a serpent, and when Egypt's magicians did the same by their enchantments, Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.

entries.title: Water turned to blood
entries.text: The river Egypt worshipped turned to blood; the fish died and the river stank.

entries.title: Frogs
entries.text: Frogs covered the land and came into Pharaoh's house and bedchamber.

entries.title: Lice
entries.text: The dust became lice. The magicians could not copy it and confessed, This is the finger of God.

entries.title: Swarms of flies
entries.text: Flies filled Egypt, but God set apart the land of Goshen where his people lived.

entries.title: Murrain on the cattle
entries.text: A grievous pestilence struck Egypt's livestock, but not one of Israel's cattle died.

entries.title: Boils
entries.text: Ashes from the furnace became boils on man and beast; the magicians could not stand before Moses.

entries.title: Hail
entries.text: The worst hailstorm in Egypt's history struck the fields; those Egyptians who feared God's word brought their servants and cattle inside.

entries.title: Locusts
entries.text: Locusts covered the face of the earth and ate every green thing the hail had left.

entries.title: Darkness
entries.meta: Egypt, but light in Goshen · Exodus 10:21–29
entries.text: Thick darkness for three days, so that no one could see another; but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

entries.title: The death of the firstborn and the Passover
entries.text: Each household of Israel killed a lamb without blemish and put its blood on the doorposts. At midnight Jehovah struck the firstborn of Egypt but passed over the houses marked with blood.

phases.title: Out of Egypt
phases.when: About 1446 BC · Egypt to the Red Sea
phases.intro: Israel left Egypt with the bones of Joseph, led by a pillar of cloud by day and of fire by night.

entries.title: The pillar of cloud and fire
entries.text: God led his people by a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, and it never departed from before them.

entries.title: The crossing of the Red Sea
entries.text: With Pharaoh's army behind them, Moses said, Stand still, and see the salvation of Jehovah. The waters parted, Israel walked through on dry ground, and the sea returned on the Egyptians.

entries.title: The Song of Moses
entries.meta: The shore of the sea · Exodus 15:1–21
entries.text: Moses and Israel sang, Jehovah is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation, and Miriam led the women with timbrels.

phases.title: To the Mountain of God
phases.when: About 1446 BC · The wilderness of Shur, Sin and Sinai
phases.intro: In the first months God taught a grumbling people to trust him day by day.

entries.title: Bitter water made sweet
entries.text: When the water was bitter, Jehovah showed Moses a tree; he cast it in and the waters were made sweet. God named himself Jehovah that healeth thee.

entries.title: Manna and quail
entries.text: God rained bread from heaven every morning for forty years, with a double portion before the Sabbath, and sent quail in the evening.

entries.title: Water from the rock
entries.text: At God's command Moses struck the rock at Horeb and water came out for the people to drink.

entries.title: Victory over Amalek
entries.text: While Moses held up his hands on the hill, with Aaron and Hur supporting them, Joshua prevailed in the battle.

entries.title: Jethro's counsel
entries.text: Jethro rejoiced at all God had done and advised Moses to appoint able men to judge the people with him.

phases.title: At Sinai
phases.intro: Israel camped before the mountain for almost a year. God gave his law, made his covenant and came to dwell among his people.

entries.title: The covenant and the Ten Commandments
entries.text: The mountain quaked and smoked as God came down in fire. He spoke the Ten Commandments, and the people trembled and stood afar off.

entries.title: The blood of the covenant
entries.text: Moses sprinkled the people with blood: Behold the blood of the covenant. The elders saw the God of Israel, and Moses went up into the cloud for forty days.

entries.title: The golden calf
entries.text: While Moses was on the mountain, Aaron made a golden calf. Moses broke the tablets, then pleaded for the people, even asking to be blotted out of God's book in their place.

entries.title: The shining face
entries.text: Moses asked to see God's glory and was shown his goodness as God proclaimed his name: merciful and gracious, slow to anger. When he came down, his face shone.

entries.title: The tabernacle filled with glory
entries.text: The tabernacle was set up exactly as God had shown, and the cloud covered it and the glory of Jehovah filled it.

phases.title: Forty Years in the Wilderness
phases.when: About 1445–1406 BC · Kadesh to the plains of Moab
phases.intro: Because the people refused to enter the land, a generation wandered and died in the wilderness. Moses led them to the edge of the promise.

entries.title: The twelve spies
entries.text: Ten spies brought an evil report; only Joshua and Caleb urged the people to trust God. Israel was sentenced to forty years in the wilderness.

entries.title: Aaron's rod buds
entries.text: After Korah's rebellion, Aaron's rod budded, blossomed and bore almonds overnight, showing God's choice of his priesthood.

entries.title: Moses strikes the rock
entries.text: Told to speak to the rock, Moses struck it twice in anger. Water came out, but God said Moses would not bring the people into the land.

entries.title: The bronze serpent
entries.meta: On the way around Edom · Numbers 21:4–9
entries.text: When fiery serpents bit the people, Moses made a serpent of brass and set it on a pole; whoever looked at it lived.

entries.title: A prophet like Moses
entries.text: In his final speeches Moses promised that God would raise up a prophet like him, and the people must listen to him.

entries.title: The death of Moses
entries.text: God showed Moses the whole land from Mount Nebo. He died there at a hundred and twenty, and there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom Jehovah knew face to face.

david.title: David
david.sub: Shepherd, king and psalmist: his life and his psalms
david.how: This companion follows David from Bethlehem to his death in Jerusalem. Where a psalm's title links it to a moment in his life, the psalm is placed beside that moment and marked with its number, so you can read his prayers in the setting that produced them. Dates are approximate: David reigned about 1010–970 BC.

phases.title: The Shepherd of Bethlehem
phases.intro: The youngest of Jesse's eight sons, keeping his father's sheep.

entries.title: Anointed by Samuel
entries.text: Jehovah looketh on the heart. Passed over by his father, David was brought in from the sheep and anointed, and the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon him from that day.

entries.title: Playing the harp for Saul
entries.text: When an evil spirit troubled Saul, David played the harp and Saul was refreshed.

entries.title: David and Goliath
entries.text: The shepherd boy faced the giant with a sling, saying the battle is Jehovah's, and struck him down with one stone.

phases.title: In Saul's Court
phases.intro: David's success made him a hero to the people and a threat to the king.

entries.title: Jonathan's covenant
entries.text: Jonathan loved David as his own soul and gave him his robe, sword and bow.

entries.title: Saul's jealousy
entries.text: The women sang, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands. Saul threw his spear at David twice.

entries.title: Escape through the window
entries.text: Michal let David down through a window when Saul sent men to watch the house and kill him. Psalm 59 is linked to that night: Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God.

phases.title: The Fugitive Years
phases.when: About 1015–1010 BC · The wilderness of Judah
phases.intro: For years David lived as an outlaw, refusing to harm the king God had anointed.

entries.title: Feigning madness at Gath
entries.text: Afraid of King Achish, David pretended to be mad and escaped. Psalm 34 recalls it: O taste and see that Jehovah is good.

entries.title: The cave of Adullam
entries.text: Some four hundred men in distress, debt and discontent gathered to David in the cave. Psalm 142 is a prayer when he was in the cave.

entries.title: Doeg betrays the priests
entries.text: Doeg the Edomite told Saul that the priests had helped David, and slew eighty-five of them. Psalm 52 answers the mighty man who boasts in mischief.

entries.title: Betrayed by the Ziphites
entries.text: The men of Ziph told Saul where David was hiding. Psalm 54: Behold, God is my helper.

entries.title: Sparing Saul in the cave
entries.text: David cut off the skirt of Saul's robe but would not lift his hand against Jehovah's anointed. Psalm 57: In the shadow of thy wings will I take refuge.

entries.title: Abigail turns away his anger
entries.text: When Nabal insulted David, his wise wife Abigail met David with gifts and kept him from shedding blood.

entries.title: David strengthened himself in God
entries.text: When raiders burned Ziklag and his own men spoke of stoning him, David strengthened himself in Jehovah and recovered everything.

phases.title: King over Judah and Israel
phases.intro: After Saul and Jonathan died at Gilboa, David became king, first over Judah and then over all Israel.

entries.title: The lament for Saul and Jonathan
entries.text: How are the mighty fallen! David mourned the king who had hunted him and the friend who had loved him.

entries.title: King at Hebron, then over all Israel
entries.text: Anointed king of Judah at Hebron, David reigned there seven years and six months, then all the tribes came and anointed him king over Israel.

entries.title: Jerusalem, the city of David
entries.text: David captured the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites and made it his capital.

entries.title: The ark comes to Jerusalem
entries.text: David danced before Jehovah with all his might as the ark was brought up with shouting and the sound of the trumpet.

entries.title: God's covenant with David
entries.text: David wanted to build God a house; instead God promised to build David a house, a kingdom and a throne established for ever.

entries.title: Kindness to Mephibosheth
entries.text: For Jonathan's sake David brought Jonathan's lame son to eat at the king's table continually.

phases.title: Sin and Its Sorrow
phases.intro: At the height of his power David fell, and trouble followed in his own house.

entries.title: Bathsheba and Uriah
entries.text: David took Uriah's wife and, to hide it, had Uriah killed in battle. The thing that David had done displeased Jehovah.

entries.title: Thou art the man
entries.text: Nathan's parable brought David to confess, I have sinned against Jehovah. Psalm 51 belongs to that moment: Create in me a clean heart, O God.

entries.title: Absalom's rebellion
entries.text: David fled barefoot up the Mount of Olives when his son seized the kingdom. Psalm 3: Jehovah, how are mine adversaries increased!

entries.title: O my son Absalom
entries.text: Absalom died in the forest of Ephraim, and David wept: would I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!

phases.title: The Last Years
phases.intro: David prepared for the temple his son would build and handed on the kingdom.

entries.title: The census and the threshing floor
entries.text: After the plague that followed his census, David bought Araunah's threshing floor for an altar, refusing to offer that which cost him nothing. The temple was later built there.

entries.title: A song of deliverance
entries.text: David sang to Jehovah, who had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies. The same song appears as Psalm 18: Jehovah is my rock, and my fortress.

entries.title: Solomon made king
entries.text: When Adonijah tried to seize the throne, David had Solomon anointed king at Gihon.

entries.title: David's charge and death
entries.text: Be thou strong therefore, and show thyself a man. David died after forty years as king and was buried in the city of David.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.sub: The journey of faith: God's promises and your notes
abraham.how: This companion follows Abraham from Ur to his burial at Machpelah. God's promises to him are numbered 1–7, because the rest of the Bible keeps returning to them: land, a great nation, and blessing for all the families of the earth. Dates follow the traditional chronology (Abraham born about 2166 BC); scholars vary.

phases.title: The Call
phases.intro: Abram's family worshipped other gods beyond the River (Joshua 24:2) until God called him out.

entries.title: Leaving Ur and Haran
entries.meta: Ur of the Chaldees; Haran · Genesis 11:27–12:5
entries.text: God said, Get thee out of thy country, promising to make him a great nation and that in thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed. Abram went at seventy-five.

entries.title: The land promised at Shechem
entries.text: Unto thy seed will I give this land. Abram built altars and called on the name of Jehovah.

entries.title: Down to Egypt
entries.text: In a famine Abram went to Egypt and passed Sarai off as his sister; God protected her and Pharaoh sent them away.

phases.title: In the Land
phases.intro: Abram grew rich in Canaan and lived as a stranger in tents.

entries.title: Lot chooses Sodom
entries.meta: Bethel; the plain of the Jordan · Genesis 13:1–18
entries.text: Abram let Lot choose first; Lot chose the plain near Sodom. God promised Abram the land as far as he could see and seed as the dust of the earth.

entries.title: Rescuing Lot; Melchizedek
entries.meta: Dan; the vale of Shaveh at Salem · Genesis 14:1–24
entries.text: Abram defeated the kings who had captured Lot. Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, blessed him, and Abram gave him a tenth.

entries.title: Counted righteous; the covenant
entries.text: Look now toward heaven, and number the stars: so shall thy seed be. Abram believed Jehovah, and he reckoned it to him for righteousness. God passed between the pieces to seal his covenant.

phases.title: Waiting for the Son
phases.intro: Years passed, and Abram and Sarai tried to bring about the promise themselves.

entries.title: Hagar and Ishmael
entries.meta: Hebron; the wilderness of Shur · Genesis 16:1–16
entries.text: At Sarai's urging Abram took Hagar, and Ishmael was born. The angel of Jehovah met Hagar in the wilderness.

entries.title: A new name and circumcision
entries.text: At ninety-nine God named him Abraham, father of a multitude, gave circumcision as the sign of the covenant, and promised a son by Sarah.

entries.title: Three visitors at Mamre
entries.text: Abraham welcomed three strangers. The Lord promised Sarah a son within a year, and when she laughed he said, Is anything too hard for Jehovah?

entries.title: Pleading for Sodom
entries.meta: Above the plain of Sodom · Genesis 18:16–19:29
entries.text: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? Abraham bargained down to ten righteous. Sodom was destroyed, but God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out.

phases.title: Isaac and the Test
phases.intro: The promised son came at last, and Abraham's faith was tested to the limit.

entries.title: Isaac is born
entries.text: Jehovah did unto Sarah as he had spoken. Abraham was a hundred years old, and Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh.

entries.title: The offering of Isaac
entries.text: God told Abraham to offer his only son. On the mountain Abraham said, God will provide himself the lamb, and God provided a ram. He renewed his oath: in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.

entries.title: Sarah's burial at Machpelah
entries.text: Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah, his only land in Canaan, to bury Sarah.

entries.title: A bride for Isaac
entries.text: Abraham's servant prayed at a well near Haran and was led to Rebekah.

entries.title: Abraham's death
entries.text: He died in a good old age, a hundred and seventy-five, and Isaac and Ishmael buried him beside Sarah.

elijah-elisha.title: Elijah and Elisha
elijah-elisha.sub: The prophets' miracle ministry and your notes
elijah-elisha.how: Elijah and Elisha served in the northern kingdom of Israel in the 800s BC, when Ahab and Jezebel promoted the worship of Baal. Their miracles are numbered in order: Elijah's 1–8 and Elisha's 9–24. Many of them anticipate the miracles of Jesus, and those links are noted. Dates are approximate.

phases.title: Elijah and the Drought
phases.intro: Ahab did more to provoke Jehovah than all the kings before him (1 Kings 16:33).

entries.title: No dew nor rain
entries.text: Elijah told Ahab that there would be neither dew nor rain but according to his word. It did not rain for three years and six months.

entries.title: Fed by ravens
entries.text: Ravens brought Elijah bread and meat morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.

entries.title: The widow's meal and oil
entries.text: A Gentile widow shared her last meal with Elijah; her jar of meal and cruse of oil did not fail until the rain came.

entries.title: The widow's son raised
entries.text: When her son died, Elijah stretched himself on the child three times and prayed, and the child revived.

phases.title: Mount Carmel and Horeb
phases.intro: Elijah challenged Israel to stop limping between two opinions.

entries.title: Fire from heaven on Carmel
entries.text: The prophets of Baal cried out all day with no answer. Elijah drenched his altar with water and prayed, and the fire of Jehovah fell and consumed it all. The people cried, Jehovah, he is God.

entries.title: Rain after the drought
entries.text: Elijah prayed seven times until a cloud like a man's hand rose from the sea, then outran Ahab's chariot to Jezreel.

entries.title: Fed by an angel; the still small voice
entries.text: Fleeing Jezebel, Elijah asked to die. An angel fed him, and on the mountain God came not in wind, earthquake or fire but in a still small voice, and told him seven thousand had not bowed to Baal.

entries.title: The call of Elisha
entries.text: Elijah threw his mantle on Elisha, who was plowing; Elisha killed his oxen, fed the people and followed him.

entries.title: Naboth's vineyard
entries.text: Jezebel had Naboth stoned so Ahab could take his vineyard. Elijah met Ahab there and pronounced judgment.

entries.title: Fire on the captains
entries.text: King Ahaziah sent soldiers to seize Elijah; fire came down on two companies of fifty. The third captain begged for mercy and was spared.

phases.title: Elijah Taken Up
phases.when: About 850 BC · Gilgal, Bethel, Jericho, the Jordan
phases.intro: Elijah's last journey, with Elisha refusing to leave him.

entries.title: The Jordan parted
entries.text: Elijah struck the water with his mantle, and the two crossed on dry ground.

entries.title: Chariots of fire
entries.text: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit. A chariot of fire and horses of fire parted them, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

phases.title: Elisha's Ministry
phases.when: About 850–795 BC · Jericho, Shunem, Samaria, Dothan
phases.intro: Elisha served for some fifty years. Many of his miracles were acts of mercy to ordinary people.

entries.title: The Jordan parted again
entries.text: Elisha struck the water with Elijah's mantle, asking, Where is Jehovah, the God of Elijah? and the river parted.

entries.title: The waters of Jericho healed
entries.text: Elisha threw salt into the spring, and the bad water was healed.

entries.title: The widow's oil
entries.meta: Among the sons of the prophets · 2 Kings 4:1–7
entries.text: A prophet's widow poured her one pot of oil into every vessel she could borrow, and sold it to pay her debt.

entries.title: A son for the Shunammite
entries.text: A woman who made a room for Elisha was promised a son, and the next year she held him.

entries.title: The Shunammite's son raised
entries.text: When the boy died, Elisha shut the door, prayed and stretched himself on the child, and he sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

entries.title: Death in the pot
entries.text: Wild gourds poisoned the prophets' stew; Elisha threw in meal and there was no harm in the pot.

entries.title: A hundred men fed
entries.text: Twenty barley loaves fed a hundred men, and they left some over, according to the word of Jehovah.

entries.title: Naaman healed of leprosy
entries.text: The Syrian commander dipped seven times in the Jordan, and his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. He confessed there is no God in all the earth but in Israel.

entries.title: Gehazi's leprosy
entries.text: Elisha's servant took Naaman's gifts by lying, and Naaman's leprosy clung to him.

entries.title: The floating axe head
entries.text: A borrowed axe head fell into the water; Elisha threw in a stick and the iron swam.

entries.title: Syria's plans revealed
entries.text: Elisha told the king of Israel the words the king of Syria spoke in his bedchamber.

entries.title: The hills full of horses and chariots
entries.text: Surrounded by a Syrian army, Elisha said, They that are with us are more than they that are with them, and his servant's eyes were opened.

entries.title: The Syrian army blinded
entries.text: Elisha led the blinded soldiers into Samaria, then had the king feed them and send them home.

entries.title: Food in the famine foretold
entries.text: In a terrible siege Elisha foretold cheap flour by the next day; four lepers found the Syrian camp abandoned.

entries.title: Victories over Syria foretold
entries.text: On his deathbed Elisha had King Joash strike the ground with arrows, foretelling three victories over Syria.

entries.title: Life from Elisha's bones
entries.text: After Elisha's death, a dead man thrown into his grave touched his bones and revived and stood up.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.sub: From the pit to the palace: dreams, suffering and providence
joseph.how: This companion follows Joseph, Jacob's eleventh son, from Canaan to Egypt. The dreams in his story are numbered 1–6: his own two, the two he interpreted in prison, and Pharaoh's two. Many Christians have seen in Joseph a picture of Christ, rejected by his brothers and exalted to save them. Dates follow the traditional chronology.

phases.title: The Favored Son
phases.intro: Jacob loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age.

entries.title: The coat of many colors
entries.text: Joseph brought a bad report of his brothers, and Jacob gave him a special coat. His brothers hated him and could not speak peaceably to him.

entries.title: The sheaves bow down
entries.text: Joseph dreamed that his brothers' sheaves bowed down to his sheaf.

entries.title: The sun, moon and stars
entries.text: In a second dream the sun, moon and eleven stars bowed to him. Even his father rebuked him, but kept the saying in mind.

entries.title: Sold into slavery
entries.text: His brothers threw him into a pit and sold him to Ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver, then showed Jacob his coat dipped in blood.

phases.title: Slave and Prisoner
phases.intro: Jehovah was with Joseph, even in Potiphar's house and in prison.

entries.title: In Potiphar's house
entries.text: Joseph prospered as a slave, and Potiphar put him in charge of everything.

entries.title: Falsely accused
entries.text: He refused Potiphar's wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God? She lied about him, and he was thrown into prison.

entries.title: The cupbearer's dream
entries.text: Joseph told the cupbearer he would be restored in three days, and asked to be remembered. The cupbearer was restored, but forgot him.

entries.title: The baker's dream
entries.text: Joseph told the baker that in three days Pharaoh would hang him, and it happened as he said.

phases.title: Ruler of Egypt
phases.intro: At thirty, after thirteen years of slavery and prison, Joseph stood before Pharaoh.

entries.title: Pharaoh's dreams: cattle and ears of grain
entries.text: Seven fat cows eaten by seven lean, and seven full ears swallowed by seven thin. Joseph said, It is not in me: God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace, and foretold seven years of plenty and seven of famine.

entries.title: Set over all Egypt
entries.text: Pharaoh made Joseph second only to himself, gave him a ring and a chain of gold, and Joseph stored grain through the years of plenty.

phases.title: The Brothers and the Family
phases.intro: The famine drove Jacob's sons to Egypt, and to the brother they had betrayed.

entries.title: The brothers bow down
entries.text: Ten brothers came to buy grain and bowed before Joseph, not knowing him. He tested them and kept Simeon.

entries.title: Benjamin and the silver cup
entries.text: When Benjamin was accused, Judah offered himself as a slave in his place.

entries.title: I am Joseph
entries.text: Joseph wept and made himself known: God did send me before you to preserve life.

entries.title: Jacob comes to Egypt
entries.text: God told Jacob, Fear not to go down into Egypt; I will there make of thee a great nation. Joseph fell on his father's neck and wept.

entries.title: God meant it for good
entries.text: After Jacob died, Joseph comforted his frightened brothers: ye meant evil against me; but God meant it for good.

entries.title: Joseph's bones
entries.text: Joseph died at a hundred and ten and made Israel promise to carry his bones to the promised land.

peter.title: Peter
peter.sub: Fisherman, apostle and shepherd of the flock
peter.how: This companion follows Simon Peter from the Sea of Galilee to Rome. The miracles God did through Peter in Acts are numbered 1–5, and his two letters are marked 1P and 2P where they fit in his life. The final part gathers what early church writers say about his last years; it is marked as tradition, not Scripture. Dates are approximate.

phases.title: The Fisherman Called
phases.when: About AD 27 · Bethsaida, Capernaum, the Sea of Galilee
phases.intro: Simon son of John, a fisherman from Bethsaida, lived in Capernaum with his wife and his brother Andrew.

entries.title: Brought to Jesus by Andrew
entries.text: Andrew told his brother, We have found the Messiah. Jesus looked at Simon and said, thou shalt be called Cephas (which is by interpretation, Peter), meaning rock.

entries.title: The great catch of fish
entries.text: After a night of catching nothing, Simon let down the nets at Jesus' word and they began to break. He fell at Jesus' knees: Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord. Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.

entries.title: His mother-in-law healed
entries.text: Jesus took her by the hand, the fever left her, and she served them. Peter's house became a base for Jesus' Galilean ministry.

entries.title: Named first of the Twelve
entries.text: In every list of the apostles, Simon, who is called Peter, comes first.

phases.title: Walking with Jesus
phases.intro: Peter was one of the inner three, with James and John, and often spoke for the Twelve.

entries.title: Walking on the water
entries.text: Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water toward Jesus, then saw the wind and began to sink. Jesus caught him: O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?

entries.title: Lord, to whom shall we go?
entries.text: When many disciples turned back, Peter answered, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.

entries.title: Thou art the Christ
entries.text: Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, and Jesus spoke of building his church on this rock. Moments later Peter rebuked Jesus for speaking of the cross and was told, Get thee behind me, Satan.

entries.title: The transfiguration
entries.text: Peter saw Jesus shining with Moses and Elijah and offered to make three tabernacles. A voice from the cloud said, This is my beloved Son; hear ye him.

entries.title: The coin in the fish's mouth
entries.text: Jesus sent Peter to catch a fish, and in its mouth he found a shekel to pay the temple tax for them both.

entries.title: How oft shall I forgive?
entries.text: Peter suggested seven times; Jesus answered, Until seventy times seven.

phases.title: The Last Week
phases.intro: Peter promised to die with Jesus, and that same night denied him.

entries.title: Washed by Jesus
entries.text: Peter protested, Thou shalt never wash my feet. If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.

entries.title: Sleeping in Gethsemane
entries.text: Jesus asked Peter, James and John to watch with him, but they slept. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

entries.title: The sword and the servant's ear
entries.text: Peter drew a sword and cut off the ear of Malchus, the high priest's servant. Jesus told him to put up the sword, and healed the ear.

entries.title: Three denials
entries.text: Three times Peter denied knowing Jesus. The cock crew, the Lord turned and looked upon Peter, and he went out and wept bitterly.

phases.title: Restored
phases.intro: The risen Lord sought out the disciple who had failed him.

entries.title: Running to the empty tomb
entries.text: Peter and John ran to the tomb; Peter went in and saw the linen cloths lying and the napkin rolled up by itself.

entries.title: The Lord appeared to Simon
entries.text: The disciples said, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon. Paul lists this among the first resurrection appearances.

entries.title: Feed my sheep
entries.text: After another miraculous catch and breakfast by the fire, Jesus asked Peter three times, Lovest thou me? and three times gave him the charge to feed his sheep, then spoke of the death by which he would glorify God.

phases.title: Leader of the Jerusalem Church
phases.when: AD 30–44 · Jerusalem, Samaria, Lydda, Joppa, Caesarea
phases.intro: In the first chapters of Acts, Peter is the church's leading spokesman.

entries.title: Choosing Matthias
entries.text: Peter led the hundred and twenty in choosing a witness to take Judas' place.

entries.title: The sermon at Pentecost
entries.text: Filled with the Spirit, Peter preached that God had made Jesus both Lord and Christ. About three thousand were baptized.

entries.title: The lame man healed
entries.meta: The Beautiful Gate of the temple · Acts 3:1–10
entries.text: Silver and gold have I none; but what I have, that give I thee. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.

entries.title: Before the council
entries.text: Arrested for preaching, Peter declared, in none other is there salvation. The council saw the boldness of unlearned men and took knowledge that they had been with Jesus.

entries.title: Ananias and Sapphira
entries.text: When a couple lied about their gift, Peter exposed it and both fell dead, and great fear came on the church.

entries.title: Healed by his shadow
entries.text: The sick were laid in the streets so that at least Peter's shadow might fall on them, and they were healed every one.

entries.title: Aeneas healed
entries.text: Aeneas, eight years bedridden, rose at Peter's word: Jesus Christ healeth thee.

entries.title: Tabitha raised
entries.text: Peter knelt and prayed beside the body of Tabitha, a disciple full of good works, and said, Tabitha, arise. She opened her eyes.

entries.title: The vision and Cornelius
entries.text: A vision of a sheet of animals taught Peter not to call any man common or unclean. At Cornelius' house the Spirit fell on Gentiles as they listened, and Peter baptized them.

entries.title: Freed from prison by an angel
entries.text: After Herod killed James, he imprisoned Peter. While the church prayed, an angel led Peter out through an iron gate that opened of its own accord.

phases.title: Later Ministry and Letters
phases.intro: Peter traveled, worked alongside Paul and others, and wrote to scattered believers.

entries.title: At the Jerusalem council
entries.text: Peter reminded the council that God made no distinction between Jew and Gentile: we believe that we shall be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus.

entries.title: Rebuked at Antioch
entries.text: When Peter drew back from eating with Gentiles, Paul resisted him to the face.

entries.title: First letter of Peter
entries.text: Writing with Silvanus to believers scattered in Asia Minor, Peter encouraged them in suffering with a living hope.

entries.title: Second letter of Peter
entries.meta: Near the end of his life · 2 Peter 1:12–21
entries.text: Knowing that the putting off of my tabernacle cometh swiftly, Peter urged believers to grow in grace and to remember the prophetic word.

phases.title: Church Tradition
phases.intro: These accounts come from early Christian writers, not from the Bible.

entries.title: Mark's Gospel and Peter
entries.text: Papias (early 100s) wrote that Mark, Peter's interpreter, wrote down what Peter remembered of Jesus' words and deeds.

entries.title: Death in Rome
entries.text: Early writers such as Clement of Rome (about AD 96) and later Eusebius say Peter was martyred in Rome under Nero, about AD 64–67; later tradition adds that he was crucified upside down.

john.title: John
john.sub: Son of thunder, beloved disciple and seer of Patmos
john.how: This companion follows John, son of Zebedee, from his father's fishing boat to the island of Patmos. The five books linked with him are marked: Jn (his Gospel), 1J, 2J, 3J (his letters) and Rev (Revelation). The Gospel does not name its author but refers to the disciple whom Jesus loved; the church has identified him as John from the earliest times. The final part, marked as tradition, gathers what early writers say about his later life.

phases.title: Called from the Nets
phases.when: About AD 27 · The Sea of Galilee
phases.intro: John and his brother James were partners with Simon Peter in a fishing business.

entries.title: Following Jesus
entries.text: Jesus called James and John as they mended their nets; they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants and went after him.

entries.title: Sons of thunder
entries.text: Jesus surnamed the brothers Boanerges, which is, Sons of thunder.

entries.title: At the raising of Jairus' daughter
entries.text: John was one of only three allowed into the room when Jesus raised the girl.

phases.title: Learning Love
phases.intro: The thunder had to be tamed. John's early zeal shows in several episodes.

entries.title: On the mountain of transfiguration
entries.text: John saw Jesus' glory with Peter and James.

entries.title: Forbidding another who cast out demons
entries.text: John reported stopping a man who cast out demons in Jesus' name; Jesus said, he that is not against us is for us.

entries.title: Fire on a Samaritan village?
entries.text: When a village refused Jesus, James and John asked to call down fire from heaven. Jesus turned and rebuked them.

entries.title: Seats of glory
entries.meta: On the road to Jerusalem · Mark 10:35–45
entries.text: James and John asked to sit at Jesus' right and left in his glory. He spoke of a cup to drink and of the Son of man who came to give his life a ransom for many.

phases.title: The Beloved Disciple
phases.intro: In John's Gospel the disciple whom Jesus loved is closest to him at the cross and the tomb.

entries.title: Leaning on Jesus' breast
entries.text: At the supper the disciple whom Jesus loved asked, Lord, who is it? and was shown who would betray him.

entries.title: Behold, thy mother
entries.text: From the cross Jesus entrusted his mother to the beloved disciple, who took her into his own home.

entries.title: He saw, and believed
entries.text: Outrunning Peter to the tomb, John went in, saw the grave clothes, and believed.

entries.title: It is the Lord
entries.text: John was first to recognize the risen Jesus on the shore. The closing verses say this disciple bore witness of these things and wrote them.

phases.title: Pillar of the Church
phases.intro: With Peter, John led the church in its first years.

entries.title: The lame man and the council
entries.text: John was with Peter when the lame man was healed and stood with him before the council: we cannot but speak the things which we saw and heard.

entries.title: Sent to Samaria
entries.text: The apostles sent Peter and John to the new believers in Samaria, who received the Holy Spirit when they laid hands on them; the brother who once wanted fire on Samaria now brought blessing.

entries.title: A pillar in Jerusalem
entries.text: Paul names James, Cephas and John as reputed pillars who gave him the right hand of fellowship.

phases.title: The Writings
phases.when: About AD 85–95 · Ephesus and Patmos (by tradition)
phases.intro: The five books linked with John are among the last written in the New Testament.

entries.title: The Gospel of John
entries.text: Written that ye may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye may have life in his name.

entries.title: First letter of John
entries.text: That which we have heard, that which we have seen with our eyes … declare we unto you. God is love, and he that abideth in love abideth in God.

entries.title: Second and third letters
entries.text: The elder writes to the elect lady and to Gaius about walking in truth and love, and about welcoming true teachers.

entries.title: The Revelation on Patmos
entries.text: Exiled for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus, John saw the risen Christ among the lampstands and received the visions of Revelation.

phases.title: Church Tradition
phases.intro: These accounts come from early Christian writers, not from the Bible.

entries.title: Ephesus and old age
entries.text: Irenaeus (about AD 180), who had heard Polycarp, John's disciple, says John lived in Ephesus until the time of Trajan (AD 98–117), outliving all the other apostles.

paul.title: Paul
paul.sub: Pharisee, persecutor and apostle to the Gentiles
paul.how: This companion follows Saul of Tarsus from Jerusalem's schools to a Roman prison. His thirteen letters are marked where they fit in his life (for example Gal, Rom, Phil), following a commonly held order; scholars date some of them differently. The final part, marked as tradition, gathers what early writers say about his death. Dates are approximate.

phases.title: Saul the Pharisee
phases.intro: A Jew of the tribe of Benjamin, born a Roman citizen in Tarsus of Cilicia.

entries.title: Born and trained
entries.text: Brought up in Jerusalem at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict manner of the law.

entries.title: At Stephen's death
entries.text: The witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul, who consented to Stephen's death and then laid waste the church.

phases.title: Conversion and Early Years
phases.when: About AD 34–46 · Damascus, Arabia, Jerusalem, Tarsus, Antioch
phases.intro: The persecutor became a preacher of the faith he had tried to destroy.

entries.title: The light on the Damascus road
entries.text: A light from heaven flashed around him and a voice said, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? Blinded, he was led into Damascus.

entries.title: Ananias and baptism
entries.text: The Lord sent Ananias to lay hands on him, calling Saul a chosen vessel to bear his name before the Gentiles. Scales fell from his eyes and he was baptized.

entries.title: Arabia and escape in a basket
entries.text: Paul went away into Arabia and returned to Damascus, where he was let down through the wall in a basket to escape.

entries.title: Barnabas vouches for him
entries.text: The disciples feared him until Barnabas brought him to the apostles. When his life was threatened, they sent him to Tarsus.

entries.title: Teaching at Antioch
entries.text: Barnabas brought Saul to Antioch, where they taught for a year and the disciples were first called Christians.

phases.title: The First Journey
phases.intro: The church at Antioch sent Barnabas and Saul out on the first missionary journey.

entries.title: Sent out from Antioch
entries.text: Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.

entries.title: Elymas blinded; Sergius Paulus believes
entries.text: Saul, who is also called Paul, rebuked the sorcerer Elymas, who was struck blind, and the proconsul believed.

entries.title: Turning to the Gentiles
entries.text: When the synagogue rejected the message, Paul and Barnabas said, lo, we turn to the Gentiles, quoting Isaiah: a light of the Gentiles.

entries.title: Healing at Lystra; stoned
entries.text: Paul healed a man lame from birth, and the crowd hailed them as gods. Later Paul was stoned and left for dead, but rose up and went on.

entries.title: Letter to the Galatians
entries.meta: Antioch (about AD 48–49, on one common view) · Galatians 2:15–21
entries.text: Paul defended justification by faith in Christ apart from the works of the law.

entries.title: The Jerusalem council
entries.text: The apostles and elders agreed that Gentile believers need not be circumcised.

phases.title: The Second Journey
phases.intro: With Silas, and later Timothy and Luke, Paul crossed into Europe.

entries.title: The Macedonian call
entries.text: In a vision a man of Macedonia pleaded, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.

entries.title: Lydia and the jailer
entries.text: Lydia believed by the riverside. Beaten and jailed, Paul and Silas sang hymns at midnight; an earthquake opened the doors and the jailer asked, what must I do to be saved?

entries.title: At the Areopagus
entries.text: Paul proclaimed the unknown God, in whom we live, and move, and have our being, and spoke of the resurrection.

entries.title: Eighteen months in Corinth
entries.text: Paul made tents with Priscilla and Aquila and taught in Corinth; the Lord told him in a vision, I have much people in this city.

entries.title: Letters to the Thessalonians
entries.text: From Corinth Paul wrote to the young church he had left behind, encouraging them about those who had died and the Lord's coming.

phases.title: The Third Journey
phases.intro: Paul spent nearly three years in Ephesus, and wrote several of his greatest letters.

entries.title: Two years in the school of Tyrannus
entries.text: All Asia heard the word, special miracles were done by Paul's hands, and believers burned their books of magic.

entries.title: Letters to the Corinthians
entries.text: Paul corrected divisions and disorder, wrote of love and the resurrection, and later defended his ministry from Macedonia.

entries.title: The riot of the silversmiths
entries.text: Demetrius stirred the city against Paul, and the crowd shouted for two hours, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

entries.title: Letter to the Romans
entries.text: Before going to Jerusalem Paul wrote his fullest account of the gospel: the righteousness of God revealed from faith unto faith.

entries.title: Eutychus raised
entries.text: A young man fell asleep during Paul's long sermon and fell from a third-story window; Paul embraced him and he was brought alive.

entries.title: Farewell to the Ephesian elders
entries.text: I hold not my life of any account as dear unto myself, so that I may accomplish my course. They wept and kissed him.

phases.title: Arrest and Prison
phases.when: About AD 57–62 · Jerusalem, Caesarea, the voyage, Rome
phases.intro: Paul was arrested in Jerusalem and spent some five years in custody.

entries.title: Arrested in the temple
entries.text: Accused of bringing a Gentile into the temple, Paul was seized by a mob and rescued by Roman soldiers, then told his conversion story from the stairs.

entries.title: Two years in Caesarea
entries.text: Paul defended himself before Felix, Festus and King Agrippa, and appealed to Caesar.

entries.title: Shipwreck and Malta
entries.text: A storm wrecked the ship, but all 276 aboard reached land safely as an angel had told Paul. On Malta a viper fastened on his hand without harm, and he healed the father of Publius.

entries.title: Under house arrest in Rome
entries.text: Paul lived two years in his own hired dwelling, preaching the kingdom of God with all boldness, none forbidding him.

entries.title: The prison letters
entries.text: As the prisoner of Christ Jesus, Paul wrote Ephesians, Colossians and Philemon, sent with Tychicus, and Philippians, with its joy in the Lord.

phases.title: Last Years
phases.intro: The pastoral letters suggest Paul was released, traveled again, and was later imprisoned a second time.

entries.title: Letters to Timothy and Titus
entries.text: Paul instructed his co-workers on leading the churches in Ephesus and Crete: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.

entries.title: I have finished the course
entries.text: In his last letter, with Luke alone beside him, Paul wrote: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith.

phases.title: Church Tradition
phases.intro: These accounts come from early Christian writers, not from the Bible.

entries.title: Martyred in Rome
entries.text: Clement of Rome (about AD 96) says Paul bore witness before rulers and reached the limits of the West; Eusebius records that he was beheaded in Rome under Nero, as a Roman citizen, about AD 67.
